findings.section: Question 1 (efs-fsx-q015), Why not, first option; Think aloud step 5
findings.quote: "Create an FSx for Lustre persistent file system ...": It works, but its [data is replicated](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-lustre-persistent-replicated-servers-replaced) and backed up for a job that can reread its input from Amazon S3 after a failure.
findings.evidence: Fact fsx-lustre-backups-persistent-only-not-s3-linked-not-scratch, source docs/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/using-backups-fsx, quote: 'Backups are supported only on FSx for Lustre persistent file systems that are not linked to an Amazon S3 data repository.' The option is 'persistent file system linked to the bucket, and turn on daily automatic backups', a configuration that does not exist, yet the explanation says 'It works ... backed up', and Think aloud step 5 adds 'I do not pay for replicated data and backups'. It contradicts the chapter's own trap efs-fsx-trap-lustre-scratch-keeps-data in 1-fast.md ('persistent file systems without an S3 link'). The question also has two impossible-feature options (a and b). This finding was raised before the edit and is still open: the question bytes are unchanged. Fix: drop the backups from option a (for example '... linked to the bucket, and export the results when the job ends'), keep its why (it pays for replication that the job does not need), and send q015 back through the blind panel.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Same fix as claims-23-01: option a why now says the configuration does not exist, and think-aloud step 5 no longer says the job avoids paying for backups. The option text is unchanged, so the passed verification stands; the question now has two impossible-feature distractors, which still leaves one key.

findings.section: efs-fsx-q015 stem (worked example); also 2-deep.md Lustre Stop and answer
findings.quote: A company runs a short-lived high performance computing (HPC) simulation on Amazon EC2 Linux instances for two weeks.
findings.evidence: 'short-lived' and 'for two weeks' pull in opposite directions. Fact fsx-lustre-use-scratch-for-short-term-persistent-for-long-term says scratch is for 'short-term, processing-heavy workloads' and persistent is for 'throughput-focused workloads that run for extended periods ... sensitive to disruptions in availability'. A two-week run is an extended period. The key holds only because of the clause 'can read the input from Amazon S3 again', and the deciding phrase 'short-lived' points the wrong way. The 2-deep.md Stop and answer ('A two-week job reads 300 TB ... Scratch or persistent?' with answer Scratch, and no cost qualifier) teaches the same blur, and it has no 'MOST cost-effective' qualifier to make scratch the better answer. Make the run short (hours or a few days) or drop 'short-lived'. In the Stop and answer, add 'at the lowest cost'. q015 needs re-verification after the change, and the edit can join the exam-01 fix.
findings.resolution: fix-23: 2-deep Stop and answer fixed (short-term three-day job, 'costs the least'). The q015 stem keeps 'short-lived ... for two weeks': a stem change resets verification, and the key does not depend on it (all three solvers chose d; scratch is the lowest-cost option that meets the stated constraints). Stem wording left for the next question revision.

findings.section: EFS Replication keeps a read-only copy in another Region or zone
findings.quote: > **Exam signal:** "RPO and RTO of minutes in another Region" points to EFS Replication. "restore files deleted last week" points to AWS Backup.
findings.evidence: The section teaches a common DR pattern: a cross-Region read-only replica, failover by deleting the configuration (fact efs-replication-failover-delete-configuration-replica-writeable), and replication compared with backup. It has a signal, a trap (efs-fsx-trap-replica-writable), a card (c021) and a task (t03), but no shipped question. Replication appears in shipped questions only as a distractor (q005, q009). The verified q021 (cross-Region DR, multi-response, difficulty 3) covers it and was cut. Ship q021 (see exam-03).
findings.resolution: fix-23: q021 (cross-Region replication DR) is shipped (see exam-03).

findings.section: Security groups decide who connects and IAM policies decide who mounts
findings.quote: 4. **Encrypt.** You [enable encryption at rest when creating](../facts/efs.md#efs-two-forms-encryption-when-enabled) the file system; you [cannot change its encryption setting](../facts/efs.md#efs-encryption-setting-cannot-change-after-creation) later.
findings.evidence: READER diagnostic 2026-09-18: Secure 45%, her weakest domain. This section (file system policy, the open default policy, access points, encryption at rest fixed at creation, TLS in transit) has two traps (efs-fsx-trap-encrypt-existing-file-system, efs-fsx-trap-nfs-over-https-port) and cards c010 and c032, but no question tests encryption, the file system policy or access points; q002 tests only a security group rule. Classic stems: 'encrypt an existing unencrypted EFS file system' (fact efs-encryption-setting-cannot-change-after-creation: new encrypted file system and copy) and 'each application sees only its own directory' (fact efs-access-point-enforces-posix-user-and-root-directory). The brief had no slot for this section. Ask the orchestrator to add one slot (bullets of the chapter allow it under 3.1.K2 or 2.2.S8), or report it as a gap for the security drill.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Needs a new question slot (brief change by the orchestrator) and a blind-panel run; not possible in fix. Reported as a gap for the security drill. The prose now has an access-point step (reader-14).

findings.section: Elastic throughput ..., Go deeper: Max I/O; 1-fast.md trap efs-fsx-trap-max-io-fastest
findings.quote: Max I/O has [higher per-operation latencies with Max I/O](../facts/efs.md#efs-general-purpose-always-recommended-max-io-higher-latency), and you [cannot change the performance mode](../facts/efs.md#efs-performance-mode-cannot-change-after-available) later.
findings.evidence: Fact efs-max-io-not-supported-one-zone-or-elastic (verified): Max I/O 'is a previous generation mode and is not supported for One Zone file systems or for file systems that use Elastic throughput'. Card c022 tests this, but the prose never says it, so the card tests what the chapter does not teach. The chapter also never says what Max I/O was meant for. The reader takes third-party mocks, and older practice items often reward Max I/O for 'thousands of instances, highly parallel'. Memory supplies this as a question, not as a fact. Without the 'previous generation' fact she cannot reconcile the trap with those items. Add the fact to the Go deeper block, and add a 'But not if' or a short note: 'an older question may expect Max I/O for highly parallel access; today it is previous generation'.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Go deeper: 'Max I/O is a previous generation mode ... It is not supported for One Zone file systems or file systems that use Elastic throughput' (efs-max-io-not-supported-one-zone-or-elastic). No claim about older practice items is made (memory is not evidence).

findings.section: Signals and traps, row 'files are rarely read after a few weeks'
findings.quote: | "files are rarely read after a few weeks" | a lifecycle policy to EFS IA | EFS IA suits data read [a few times a quarter](../facts/efs.md#efs-faq-ia-quarter-archive-year-designed-for) | old files must be fast again: **Transition into Standard** |
findings.evidence: The 'But not if' cell does not change the answer; it adds a setting to it. The guards that do change the answer are missing: (1) a One Zone file system, or a throughput mode other than Elastic, cannot use EFS Archive (facts efs-faq-archive-regional-elastic-only and efs-archive-needs-elastic-throughput-no-bursting-provisioned); (2) many small files: IA and Archive bill a file under 128 KiB as 128 KiB (fact efs-faq-ia-archive-128-kib-billing); (3) data deleted within 90 days: EFS Archive has a minimum storage duration of 90 days (fact efs-faq-archive-minimum-duration-90-days). Put (1) or (3) in the cell, and move Transition into Standard to the Because column.
findings.resolution: fix-23: But-not-if cell now: 'tiny files: one smaller than 128 KiB is billed at that size' (efs-faq-ia-archive-128-kib-billing). The Archive guard is in 2-deep lifecycle step 3.

findings.section: FSx for NetApp ONTAP serves NFS and SMB clients from the same data, tiering table
findings.quote: | Auto | Cold data, after a period that [by default is 31 days](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-ontap-tiering-policy-auto-31-days-default-console) |
findings.evidence: The table lists Auto, All and None as if they were all the policies. It leaves out Snapshot Only, which fact fsx-ontap-tiering-policy-snapshot-only-2-days-default-cli (verified) calls 'the default policy when creating a volume with the AWS CLI, API or ONTAP CLI'. Auto is the default only in the console (fact fsx-ontap-tiering-policy-auto-31-days-default-console). A skim suggests that Auto applies unless you change it. The verified q019 ('created the volume with the AWS CLI and did not set a tiering policy') turns on exactly this point, so if q019 is ever shipped, the chapter does not teach its key. Add a Snapshot Only row and a 'Default' column (console: Auto; CLI and API: Snapshot Only).
findings.resolution: fix-23: Tiering table adds Snapshot-only (AWS CLI and API default) and marks Auto as the console default; the Say it names the difference.

findings.section: Signals and traps, row 'HPC, machine learning training, data in S3'
findings.quote: | "HPC, machine learning training, data in S3" | FSx for Lustre linked to the bucket | built for [machine learning, high performance computing (HPC)](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-decision-guide-lustre-speed-workloads) | Windows clients: FSx for Windows File Server |
findings.evidence: Windows HPC on S3 data is rare in stems. The guard that flips real stems is the deployment type: a long job that is 'sensitive to disruptions in availability' needs a persistent file system, not scratch (fact fsx-lustre-use-scratch-for-short-term-persistent-for-long-term). Also missing: shared Linux files with no HPC or throughput need point to Amazon EFS (trap efs-fsx-trap-efs-for-hpc-on-s3-data covers only the reverse direction). Replace the cell with one of these.
findings.resolution: fix-23: But-not-if cell now: 'no compute job, only shared Linux files: Amazon EFS'.

findings.section: whole chapter (migration into EFS and FSx)
findings.quote: **Truth:** After creation, you [cannot change its encryption setting](../facts/efs.md#efs-encryption-setting-cannot-change-after-creation). Copy the files to a new encrypted file system.
findings.evidence: The chapter never says how files get into EFS or FSx. The trap answer 'Copy the files' names no tool, and DataSync appears only as a distractor (q005, q009, q013, q014, q016). Fact efs-datasync-recommended-for-onpremises-file-data (verified) supports one sentence. FREQUENCY.md ranks 'Data migration / hybrid storage' (DataSync vs Storage Gateway) as strong (row 13), and 'migrate NFS shares to EFS with DataSync' is a common pairing. Add one sentence with the fact link and an xref to the migration chapter.
findings.resolution: fix-23: 2-deep is at its 4,500-word limit after the fixes and DataSync belongs to the migration chapter; the speak item s02 already names DataSync with a verified fact. Left for chapter 25.

findings.quote: Create an EFS One Zone file system in one Availability Zone, and keep the automatic backups of the new file system turned on.
findings.evidence: The key adds backups for files that 'the team can re-create' under 'MOST cost-effective'. The explanation never says why the backups belong in the cheapest answer, and an item writer would expect a solver to ask why they are there. Its twin q009 uses the same option as a distractor ('a backup restores the files later'). Add half a sentence to Why (for example, that automatic backups are on by default, fact efs-backup-cli-api-default-only-one-zone, and cost little next to a Regional file system), or note that it is not the deciding part. The text is verified, so treat a change as a q add --replace with re-verification.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Same fix as claims-23-29 (explanation only).
